problem: On REVERIE, high-level short instructions give little guidance for exploration. Prior LLM-based methods are zero-shot or hard-prompt-based (NavGPT, MapGPT, MiC), error-prone, need human prompt design, and the LLM hallucinates absent objects and is biased toward certain objects.
motivation: Providing the agent with a proper navigation plan is essential for efficient goal-oriented exploration without pre-exploration. Base LLMs generate sub-instructions that mention absent objects (hallucination) or repeat certain objects (bias), leading to wrong actions. This motivates fine-tuning the LLM with navigation data and environmental feedback.
key_idea: Use a LoRA-fine-tuned Llama-2-7B (SFT on FGR2R sub-instructions, then DPO with preferences from a frozen policy's single-step action prediction) to generate a single-step instruction at each viewpoint that augments the high-level instruction fed to HM3D-DUET.
insight: Environment-feedback preference tuning adds gains beyond SFT. In the fine-tuning ablation, LoRA alone gives SPL 44.25 and LoRA+DPO gives 44.85 vs. base LLM 42.45, and LoRA beats prefix tuning. Fine-tuning and a constrained object list reduce hallucination: correct usage of visual landmarks goes from 7.37% (no object list) to 96.47% (with list) to 98.96% (LoRA + list), and the object-repetition bias is more balanced. The goal-oriented plan (LGP) alone already helps (SPL 40.58→42.04).
method: LLM Goal Planner (LGP): base Llama-2 with chain-of-thought-style three steps (goal → target object → target room chosen from the REVERIE room list); run once per episode before navigation.
Object retrieval: ODISE panoptic segmentation on the panorama, then CLIP cosine similarity to the averaged viewpoint image embeddings selects the top-5 most relevant visible objects.
LoRA Action Planner (LAP): fine-tuned Llama-2-7B-chat prompted with goal plan, high-level instruction and visible objects; generates a single-step instruction at every location on the fly.
SFT stage: LoRA (or prefix tuning) on FGR2R decomposed sub-instructions mapped to ground-truth path viewpoints via chunk view (REVERIE and R2R share trajectories).

DPO stage: LAP-generated instructions are labelled chosen/rejected by whether frozen HM3D-DUET, on the SAP task with the concatenated instruction, predicts the ground-truth next viewpoint; DPO with a frozen reference copy.
Policy: HM3D-DUET (topological map, fine/coarse encoders with dynamic fusion), unchanged, receives high-level plus generated instruction; fine-tuned on REVERIE for 20k iterations on one 3090.

setting.backbone: Llama-2-7B-chat (LoRA fine-tuned SFT+DPO, base for LGP) + HM3D-DUET policy (fine-tuned) + ODISE + CLIP
setting.training_data: FGR2R sub-instructions (R2R-derived) for SFT; DPO preference set from SAP feedback; policy uses the HM3D-DUET pre-trained model and augmented data, fine-tuned on REVERIE
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) with object features, plus ODISE/CLIP-derived visible object labels
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (topological map, global action planning) plus stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (the environment graph and ground-truth actions are used only in training/preference construction)

numbers.extra: uses HM3D-DUET pre-trained model and augmented data

numbers_note: Ablation tables report a baseline of 54.36 SR on val-unseen, which differs from Table 1's HM3D-DUET row (55.89), so they are not comparable across tables.
results: PEAP-LLM beats HM3D-DUET on REVERIE val-unseen by 4.00 SPL (44.85 vs 40.85) and 3.20 RGSPL (29.96 vs 26.76). On test-unseen it gains 2.10 SPL (40.98 vs 38.88) and 2.20 RGSPL (24.88 vs 22.68), achieving state of the art on all metrics against methods such as VER, BSG, and BEVBert.
limitations: Generating an instruction with the LLM at each location adds computational overhead; the authors suggest querying only when uncertain.
Evaluated only on REVERIE with one policy (HM3D-DUET) and one LLM (Llama-2-7B); generalization to other benchmarks is not tested.
Object detection is limited to the top-5 labels without orientation information, and the SFT data come from R2R-derived FGR2R.
